raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

MiMo-V2.6 has asymmetric K/V head dims (192 / 128), which today pins it to the DiffKV attention backends: any other `--attention-backend` is silently replaced by the DiffKV auto-pick, and the native KV-cache write would copy V with K's head width. This PR makes `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` usable for the model (opt-in, defaults unchanged) and fixes the write kernel.

## Claims

- `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` now selects unified attention for every MiMo-V2.6 layer instead of being dropped; verified on Flash (TP2, TP4, TP8) and on Pro (TP8, gsm8k n=100 parity).
- `reshape_and_cache_flash` writes V with its own head size and head stride. Symmetric callers run the same code as before: the new checks live in the asymmetric branch, and the existing kernel is byte-identical to `main`.
- Accuracy and speculative-decoding parity with the default backend (gsm8k at n=1319, MTP x3 acceptance).
- At long context prefill is 1.43x faster at 128k and 1.21x at 32k, with decode 1.17x faster per token (TPOT p50 2.94 vs 3.45 ms) and output throughput up 21-45%. At 8k with concurrency 8 the two are at parity. Measured with `--block-size 16` on both arms, which tested better than the backend's default for this shape. On Pro at TP8 the same benchmark gives 1.13x prefill and 1.66x lower inter-token latency.

## Validation

### Commands

```bash
# serve (TP4 shown; TP2/TP8 differ only in --tensor-parallel-size; the control arm drops
# --attention-backend and gets the DiffKV auto-pick)
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 270336 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.82 \
  --block-size 16 --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' \
  --disable-prefix-caching \
  --tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo

# serve bench, one cell (input/output lengths and prompt counts per the tables)
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --model XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 32 \
  --num-prompts 2 --max-concurrency 1 --num-warmups 1 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 0

# gsm8k 25-shot against the running server
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template

# tests
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k asymmetric
pytest tests/models/test_mimo_v2_attention_backend.py
```

### Bench serve

Mimo-V2.6 Flash at TP4:

| workload | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128k in / 32 out, 2 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 7633.8 ms | 5317.7 ms | -30% (1.44x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: output throughput | 4.10 tok/s | 5.96 tok/s | +45% |
| 32k in / 128 out, 4 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 890.9 ms | 738.2 ms | -17% (1.21x) |
| 32k in / 128 out: TPOT p50 | 3.45 ms | 2.94 ms | -15% |
| 32k in / 128 out: output throughput | 96.1 tok/s | 116.0 tok/s | +21% |
| 8k in / 256 out, 8 prompts, c8: ITL p50 | 8.42 ms | 8.48 ms | parity |
| 8k in / 256 out: output throughput | 929 tok/s | 947 tok/s | +2% |

On MiMo-V2.6-Pro at TP8:

| workload | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128k in / 32 out, 2 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 9665.0 ms | 8576.9 ms | -11% (1.13x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: ITL p50 | 19.52 ms | 11.77 ms | -40% (1.66x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: output throughput | 3.23 tok/s | 3.68 tok/s | +14% |

Acceptance rate:
| | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified |
|---|---|---|
| MTP acceptance, 128k (acc % / length) | 53.33 / 2.07 | 56.67 / 2.13 |
| MTP acceptance, 32k | 61.40 / 2.23 | 55.60 / 2.11 |
| MTP acceptance, 8k c8 | 57.4-60.5 | 58.2-60.3 |


### lm_eval

| checkpoint | unified | DiffKV | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flash, gsm8k n=1319 | 0.9750 / 0.9742 | 0.9719 / 0.9712 | strict / flexible |

### Needle-In-A-Haystack

Unified attention only; `--max-model-len 270336`, thinking off, greedy.

| probe | config | result |
|---|---|---|
| niah | 265,673 tokens, depths 0 / 50 / 100 % | 3/3 |

### Tests

```
# kernel fix: main's cache_kernels.cu vs this one
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k asymmetric        # 33 failed -> 33 passed
# model change: main's backend selection vs this one (either kernel)
pytest tests/models/test_mimo_v2_attention_backend.py             # 2 failed, 5 passed -> 7 passed
```

The asymmetric kernel test runs MiMo's geometry (K 192 / V 128, 4 KV heads) at both block sizes the model uses (16 and 64) over a parametrized token count, in both layouts unified attention hands the kernel, for bf16 and fp8 caches and per-tensor and per-head scales. The whole file stays green (694 passed, 602 skipped).

The model test gained two checks: the selected backend's *impl* has to be unified attention's, not just its enum; and the cache the layer writes has to match a cache built in torch, per slot, with K in the first `head_dim` columns of a row and V in the remaining `v_head_dim`. Both fail on `main`. The kernel test's buffers carry slack past the cache, so a regressed kernel fails that comparison instead of writing out of bounds.

## Details

`reshape_and_cache_flash_kernel` derived one head size, one page stride, one head stride and one element count from key/key_cache and reused all of them for the value side:

```cpp
cache_t* v_dst_h = value_dst + head * head_stride;             // K's stride
vectorize_with_alignment(value_src, value_dst, n_elems, ...);  // K's width
```

Every caller until now was symmetric, so this was invisible. Unified attention is the first caller that passes `v_head_size != head_size` (MiMo is 192 / 128, packed as one `(head_size + head_size_v)` content dim per KV head), and for it V was read at K's per-head offset, copied at K's width - 64 elements past the end of each head - and written past the end of the cache on the last slot. The asymmetric case now gets its own kernel that addresses V with the value side's own head stride and length; the existing kernel and its NHD fast path are untouched, so symmetric callers run the same code as before.

Model side: the attention backend is chosen per layer, and the gate now consults a backend capability (`supports_head_size_v`) rather than listing backend names. DiffKV declares that it can serve any K/V width relation; unified attention declares `v <= k`, because it splits the page with `split(head_size)`. A backend that cannot serve the shape still gets the previous behaviour: a warning and the DiffKV auto-pick.

Known limitations:

- Requires aiter >= 0.1.25 for the V-dim-masked unified-attention kernels; `main` pins 0.1.26.
- Unified attention serves V narrower than K, not wider (`v_head_dim > head_dim` cannot be expressed by its page split); such a request falls back to the DiffKV auto-pick with a warning.


---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

+# MiMo-V2.6 Flash: K 192 / V 128, 4 KV heads, block sizes 16 and 64 in use.
+ASYM_HEAD_SIZE = 192
+ASYM_HEAD_SIZE_V = 128
+ASYM_NUM_KV_HEADS = 4
+ASYM_BLOCK_SIZES = [16, 64]
+ASYM_NUM_TOKENS = [6, 512]
+# "unified": one page holds K's head group then V's, addressed the way ROCm
+# AITER unified attention hands the kernel (transpose(1, 2).split(head_size)).
+# "grouped": the same page content laid out per token, which gives the other
+# (page-contiguous, head-strided) stride pattern. No in-tree backend produces it
+# today; it keeps both stride shapes covered for asymmetric head dims.
+ASYM_LAYOUTS = ["unified", "grouped"]
+
+
+def test_reshape_and_cache_flash_asymmetric_tiny_head() -> None:
+    """A single small head still fills the cache correctly.
+
+    num_heads * max(head_size, v_head_size) is below one warp here, so a launch
+    that sized the block from the element count would schedule zero warps and
+    the per-head loop would never advance.
+    """
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    device = "cuda:0"
+    torch.set_default_device(device)
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+
+    num_tokens, num_heads = 4, 1
+    head_size, v_head_size = 16, 8
+    block_size, num_blocks = 16, 2
+    content = head_size + v_head_size
+
+    packed = torch.zeros(
+        num_blocks, num_heads, block_size, content, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    key_cache, value_cache = packed.transpose(1, 2).split(
+        [head_size, v_head_size], dim=-1
+    )
+    slot_mapping = torch.tensor([0, 5, 16, 31], dtype=torch.long)
+    key = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_heads, head_size, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    value = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_heads, v_head_size, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float32)
+    v_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    ops.reshape_and_cache_flash(
+        key,
+        value,
+        key_cache,
+        value_cache,
+        slot_mapping,
+        "auto",
+        k_scale,
+        v_scale,
+    )
+
+    expected_key = torch.zeros_like(key_cache)
+    expected_value = torch.zeros_like(value_cache)
+    for token, slot in enumerate(slot_mapping.tolist()):
+        block, offset = slot // block_size, slot % block_size
+        expected_key[block, offset] = key[token]
+        expected_value[block, offset] = value[token]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(key_cache, expected_key)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(value_cache, expected_value)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kv_cache_layout", ASYM_LAYOUTS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kv_scale_type", KV_SCALE_TYPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kv_cache_dtype", KV_CACHE_DTYPE)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_size", ASYM_BLOCK_SIZES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", ASYM_NUM_TOKENS)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_reshape_and_cache_flash_asymmetric_head_sizes(
+    kv_cache_layout: str,
+    kv_scale_type: str,
+    kv_cache_dtype: str,
+    block_size: int,
+    num_tokens: int,
+) -> None:
+    """V is written with its own head width and head stride.
+
+    Both layouts keep K and V in one layer buffer, so only per-head geometry
+    differs between the two sides.
+    """
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    device = "cuda:0"
+    torch.set_default_device(device)
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+
+    num_heads = ASYM_NUM_KV_HEADS
+    num_blocks = num_tokens // block_size + 2
+    content = ASYM_HEAD_SIZE + ASYM_HEAD_SIZE_V
+    # A kernel that copies K's width into V runs past the page, so leave enough
+    # slack to turn that into a failed assertion instead of an out-of-bounds
+    # write that takes the whole test process down.
+    guard = num_heads * content
+    cache_dtype = torch.uint8 if kv_cache_dtype == "fp8" else torch.bfloat16
+    # The last slot is always written: a too-wide copy would run past the end.
+    num_slots = block_size * num_blocks
+    slot_mapping = torch.randperm(num_slots - 1, device=device)[: num_tokens - 1]
+    slot_mapping = torch.cat(
+        [slot_mapping, torch.tensor([num_slots - 1], device=device)]
+    ).to(torch.long)
+
+    key = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, num_heads, ASYM_HEAD_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
+    )
+    value = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, num_heads, ASYM_HEAD_SIZE_V, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
+    )
+
+    # K and V are views of one packed layer buffer, as in vLLM.
+    content = ASYM_HEAD_SIZE + ASYM_HEAD_SIZE_V
+    if kv_cache_layout == "unified":
+        # [num_blocks, num_heads, block_size, content], split per side.
+        num_bytes = num_blocks * num_heads * block_size * content
+        buf = torch.zeros(num_bytes + guard, dtype=cache_dtype, device=device)
+        packed = buf[:num_bytes].view(num_blocks, num_heads, block_size, content)
+        key_cache, value_cache = packed.transpose(1, 2).split(
+            [ASYM_HEAD_SIZE, ASYM_HEAD_SIZE_V], dim=-1
+        )
+    else:
+        # [num_blocks, block_size, num_heads, content], K group then V group.
+        num_bytes = num_blocks * block_size * num_heads * content
+        buf = torch.zeros(num_bytes + guard, dtype=cache_dtype, device=device)
+        packed = buf[:num_bytes].view(num_blocks, block_size, num_heads, content)
+        key_cache, value_cache = packed.split(
+            [ASYM_HEAD_SIZE, ASYM_HEAD_SIZE_V], dim=-1
+        )
+
+    if kv_cache_dtype == "fp8":
+        # Compare in fp16 after dequantizing, as the symmetric case does.
+        expected_key = torch.zeros(key_cache.shape, dtype=torch.float16, device=device)
+        expected_value = torch.zeros(
+            value_cache.shape, dtype=torch.float16, device=device
+        )
+    else:
+        expected_key = torch.zeros_like(key_cache)
+        expected_value = torch.zeros_like(value_cache)
+    for token, slot in enumerate(slot_mapping.tolist()):
+        block, offset = slot // block_size, slot % block_size
+        expected_key[block, offset] = key[token]
+        expected_value[block, offset] = value[token]
+
+    scale_shape = (1,) if kv_scale_type == "tensor" else (num_heads,)
+    k_scale = torch.ones(scale_shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    v_scale = torch.ones(scale_shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+
+    ops.reshape_and_cache_flash(
+        key,
+        value,
+        key_cache,
+        value_cache,
+        slot_mapping,
+        kv_cache_dtype,
+        k_scale,
+        v_scale,
+    )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+
+    if kv_cache_dtype == "fp8":
+
+        def _dequant(cache, scale):
+            # gfx94x stores fp8 as e4m3fnuz; reinterpret with the platform dtype
+            # so the bytes are decoded the way the kernel wrote them.
+            values = cache.view(current_platform.fp8_dtype()).to(torch.float16)
+            scale = scale.to(torch.float16)
+            if scale.numel() == 1:
+                return values * scale
+            # per-attn-head scales broadcast over the head dimension
+            return values * scale.view(1, 1, -1, 1)
+
+        result_key = _dequant(key_cache, k_scale)
+        result_value = _dequant(value_cache, v_scale)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(result_key, expected_key, atol=0.001, rtol=0.1)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(result_value, expected_value, atol=0.001, rtol=0.1)
+    else:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(key_cache, expected_key)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(value_cache, expected_value)
+        # Untouched slots stay zero, and nothing is written behind the cache.
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(key_cache) == num_tokens * num_heads * ASYM_HEAD_SIZE
+        assert (
+            torch.count_nonzero(value_cache)
+            == num_tokens * num_heads * ASYM_HEAD_SIZE_V
+        )
+    assert torch.count_nonzero(buf[num_bytes:]) == 0
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", DTYPES)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MiMo-V2.6 has head_dim 192 but v_head_dim 128, so only backends that keep
+V's width out of the K path can serve it. An explicit ``--attention-backend``
+from that set has to be honored; any other request has to fall back to the
+DiffKV auto-pick with a warning rather than mount a backend that cannot serve
+the shape.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import AttentionConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import AttentionBackendEnum
+
+HEAD_DIM = 192
+V_HEAD_DIM = 128
+
+DIFFKV_BACKENDS = (
+    AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN_DIFFKV,
+    AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV,
+)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def bf16_default_dtype():
+    # Backend selection is dtype sensitive; use the dtype the model ships in.
+    default_dtype = torch.get_default_dtype()
+    torch.set_default_dtype(torch.bfloat16)
+    yield
+    torch.set_default_dtype(default_dtype)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def restore_diffkv_head_size_v():
+    """``set_head_size_v`` writes backend class state.
+
+    Leaving it modified would make these tests order dependent, so snapshot and
+    restore it on every backend that can be selected here.
+    """
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flash_attn_diffkv import (
+        FlashAttentionDiffKVBackend,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.triton_attn_diffkv import (
+        TritonAttentionDiffKVBackend,
+    )
+
+    backends = (FlashAttentionDiffKVBackend, TritonAttentionDiffKVBackend)
+    saved = [backend.head_size_v for backend in backends]
+    yield
+    for backend, head_size_v in zip(backends, saved):
+        backend.head_size_v = head_size_v
+
+
+def _build_attention(
+    backend: AttentionBackendEnum | None, v_head_dim: int = V_HEAD_DIM
+):
+    from vllm.model_executor.models.mimo_v2 import MiMoV2Attention
+
+    config = VllmConfig(attention_config=AttentionConfig(backend=backend))
+    with set_current_vllm_config(config):
+        layer = MiMoV2Attention(
+            hidden_size=512,
+            num_heads=4,
+            num_kv_heads=2,
+            head_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+            v_head_dim=v_head_dim,
+            prefix="model.layers.0.self_attn",
+        )
+    return layer
+
+
+def test_default_backend_is_diffkv(dist_init) -> None:
+    """No explicit backend: the DiffKV auto-pick is unchanged."""
+    layer = _build_attention(None)
+    assert layer.attn.backend in DIFFKV_BACKENDS
+    # V's width has to reach the layer: Attention defaults head_size_v to
+    # head_size (192), which would corrupt the output reshape and KV spec.
+    assert layer.attn.head_size_v == V_HEAD_DIM
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN is ROCm only"
+)
+def test_explicit_unified_attention_is_honored(dist_init) -> None:
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import IS_AITER_FOUND
+
+    if not IS_AITER_FOUND:
+        pytest.skip("aiter is not installed")
+
+    layer = _build_attention(AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN)
+    assert layer.attn.backend is AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN
+    # The enum alone would not catch the bug this guards: the impl has to be
+    # unified attention's, not the DiffKV one the auto-pick installs.
+    assert type(layer.attn.impl).__name__ == "RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionImpl"
+
+
+def test_explicit_diffkv_backend_is_honored(dist_init) -> None:
+    """The accept path also works for the DiffKV family, on any platform."""
+    layer = _build_attention(AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV)
+    assert layer.attn.backend is AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV
+    assert layer.attn.head_size_v == V_HEAD_DIM
+
+
+def test_explicit_symmetric_backend_falls_back_to_diffkv(dist_init) -> None:
+    """A backend that cannot take head_size_v != head_size must not be mounted."""
+    layer = _build_attention(AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN)
+    assert layer.attn.backend in DIFFKV_BACKENDS
+
+
+def test_layer_v_head_dim_reaches_the_backend(dist_init) -> None:
+    """The backend must be told V's width before its impl is built.
+
+    The DiffKV backends default to ``head_size_v = 128``, which is this model's
+    own V width, so a missing ``set_head_size_v`` call is invisible at the
+    model's geometry. That attribute is what the metadata builder and forward
+    read, so assert it carries the layer's width instead of the default.
+    """
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.triton_attn_diffkv import (
+        TritonAttentionDiffKVBackend,
+    )
+
+    _build_attention(AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV, v_head_dim=64)
+    assert TritonAttentionDiffKVBackend.head_size_v == 64
+
+
+def test_only_backends_that_can_serve_v_head_size_are_admitted() -> None:
+    """`supports_head_size_v` is what the model's gate consults."""
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flash_attn_diffkv import (
+        FlashAttentionDiffKVBackend,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.rocm_aiter_unified_attn import (
+        RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.triton_attn_diffkv import (
+        TritonAttentionDiffKVBackend,
+    )
+
+    assert FlashAttentionDiffKVBackend.supports_head_size_v(HEAD_DIM, V_HEAD_DIM)
+    assert TritonAttentionDiffKVBackend.supports_head_size_v(HEAD_DIM, V_HEAD_DIM)
+    # The packed cache is split with `split(head_size)`, so V cannot be wider.
+    assert RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend.supports_head_size_v(HEAD_DIM, V_HEAD_DIM)
+    assert not RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend.supports_head_size_v(
+        V_HEAD_DIM, HEAD_DIM
+    )
+
+
+def test_cache_write_matches_pytorch_reference(dist_init) -> None:
+    """Fill the packed cache through the impl, then compare with torch.
+
+    The layer hands the kernel two views of one layer buffer, and V has its own
+    width, so the check is what lands in that buffer: K in the first
+    ``head_dim`` slots of a row, V in the remaining ``v_head_dim``. Same shape
+    as the aiter FA check in tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_fa.py, for
+    the asymmetric case those backends cannot serve.
+    """
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import IS_AITER_FOUND
+
+    if not IS_AITER_FOUND:
+        pytest.skip("aiter is not installed")
+
+    from tests.kernels.allclose_default import get_default_atol, get_default_rtol
+
+    layer = _build_attention(AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN)
+    impl = layer.attn.impl
+    num_kv_heads = layer.num_kv_heads
+    num_tokens, block_size, num_blocks = 6, 16, 2
+
+    # One packed layer buffer per token row: [K head_dim | V v_head_dim]. The
+    # spare trailing block absorbs an over-wide write from a regressed kernel,
+    # so that fails the comparison instead of writing out of bounds.
+    packed = torch.zeros(
+        num_blocks + 1,
+        num_kv_heads,
+        block_size,
+        HEAD_DIM + V_HEAD_DIM,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+    key = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, num_kv_heads, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"
+    )
+    value = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, num_kv_heads, V_HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"
+    )
+    # Slot 31 is the last slot of the cache.
+    slot_mapping = torch.tensor([0, 5, 16, 31, 7, 17], dtype=torch.long, device="cuda")
+
+    # The impl reads only the scales off `layer`; they are not the subject here.
+    scales = torch.nn.Module()
+    scales._k_scale = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    scales._v_scale = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    impl.do_kv_cache_update(scales, key, value, packed, slot_mapping)
+
+    expected = torch.zeros_like(packed)
+    for token, slot in enumerate(slot_mapping.tolist()):
+        block, offset = divmod(slot, block_size)
+        # packed buffer is [blocks, kv_heads, block_tokens, content]
+        expected[block, :, offset, :HEAD_DIM] = key[token]
+        expected[block, :, offset, HEAD_DIM:] = value[token]
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        packed, expected, atol=get_default_atol(packed), rtol=get_default_rtol(packed)
+    )
